label: neiso 106 fossil offer
definition: KEEPER. neiso-106 is a full-span 2023/2024/2025 replay of the neiso-99 recipe with EXACTLY ONE delta: a single scalar 0.95470 (a 4.530% cut) applied to 12 markup bands of offer_curve_by_group -- committed/econ_low/econ_high of CC_REGULAR, CC_CHP, CT_PEAKER, ST_GAS. All four peak bands, every phys_*, econ_low_share, pct_peaking and the declared-neutral CT_CHP group are unchanged (verified: exactly 12 bands moved, all at the identical ratio 0.954700, zero out-of-scope moves). Applied through the rules 1 [R-STRUCT] / 13 [R-MEASURED] authorized price-tuning channel on owner direction 2026-09-06: ONE config across every scored year, declared ex ante in PREREG-neiso106-offer-level-rederived-2026-09-06.md and COMMITTED (773411e5) before the solve, never swept against the gates. || WHAT CHANGED FROM THE SUPERSEDED KEEPER 2026-09-06-neiso-105-fossil-offer: only the COEFFICIENT in the sizing division, never the target. neiso-105's 6.609% cut was sized on the pass-through the neiso-104 screen measured on ONE year (0.5247, 2025); the full span has since measured the same coefficient directly at 0.76550 -- the geometric mean of that keeper's own three in-sample price moves (-5.0592%) over the cut that produced them. The target is the SAME +3.4678% in-sample geometric-mean price bias fixed in PREREG-neiso104 section 3.1 before any LP ran, reproduced from the committed sidecars here at 0.034674 and still divided at the declared 0.034678: 0.034678 / 0.76550 = 4.530%. || THE ARM LANDS WHERE IT WAS PRE-REGISTERED, to 0.02 pp on every year. C3a mean LMP bias: 2023 -3.36% -> -1.34% (pre-registered -1.32%), 2024 -0.02% -> +1.76% (+1.77%), 2025 -1.89% -> -0.77% (-0.78%). In-sample geometric-mean bias -1.767% -> -0.124% (pre-registered -0.119%); mean absolute error 1.758% -> 1.290%. Against the pre-cut neiso-99 basis the bias moved +3.467% -> -0.124% and the MAE 3.481% -> 1.290%. || DETERMINATION CALIBRATED, criterion-for-criterion IDENTICAL to the superseded keeper: 0 FAILs; C1 (all 12/12, free 8/8), C2, C3a, C3b, C4, C6, C8 all PASS; C3c price tail/scarcity the sole ledgered caveat, carried forward unchanged in substance. THE NAMED LIVE RISK DID NOT FIRE: PREREG section 6 put C3b price duration/shape as the exposure that would take NEISO to NOT-YET by breaking rubric v3.3 guard (a), and C3b PASSES -- as the pre-registered bracketing argument expected, since 0.95470 lies strictly between two configurations that both scored C3b PASS on these same three years (neiso-99 at 1.0, neiso-105 at 0.93391). || THE FINDING THIS RUN SURFACES, worth more than the scalar: pass-through is strongly YEAR-dependent and tracks delivered gas INVERSELY and monotonically -- 1.3055 at $1.98/MMBtu (2020), 0.9525 at $2.93 (2023), 0.8138 at $3.07 (2024), 0.7061 at $4.50 (2021), 0.5269 at $6.24 (2025), 0.4126 in 2022. It is NOT depth-dependent: 2025 is the only year solved at two cut depths and reads 0.5254 at 4.53% against 0.5269 at 6.609%, a ratio of 1.0029 over a 46% change in depth. Rule 29 [R-SCREEN] selects the screen year by LARGEST ABSOLUTE FOOTPRINT, which for a multiplier on HR x fuel is the highest-gas year, which is the LOWEST pass-through year -- so the prescribed screen year yields the least representative coefficient. The receipt: neiso-104 declared 0.765 from an across-year gas elasticity and recorded that identification REFUTED when its 2025 screen measured 0.525; the full-span figure is 0.7655, i.e. the refuted number was right to within 0.07%. What was wrong was reading a one-year screen as a measurement of the span. Filed as an owner ask (PREREG section 7); NOT acted on by this lane. || AN UNEXPECTED CROSS-CHECK, reported because it strengthens a claim this lane had to state weakly: the 2025 solve is BIT-IDENTICAL to the neiso-104 screen arm that rule 29(c) required to be deleted -- same P0 objective 3,554,608,783.6457 to 13 significant figures and the same 188,740 / 59,473 simplex iteration counts on both passes -- despite running on highspy 1.14.0 / pandas 3.0.3 / pydantic 2.13.4 against that arm's 1.15.1 / 3.0.5 / 2.13.5. That independently confirms the declared scalar reproduces neiso-104's config exactly, reconstructs the deleted screen result inside a registrable bundle, and upgrades ADDENDUM-neiso104-env-correction's '4 dp on load-weighted price' to bit-identity on the LP itself. || DISCLOSED RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE FOUND: (1) this is the THIRD sizing of this scalar (4.53% -> 6.609% -> 4.530%) and PREREG-neiso105 section 3 pre-committed it would not move again in either direction; that lane-level stop rule is overridden by the owner direction, not reasoned away -- though neiso-105's OWN matrix stamp had already drawn the line, calling a full-span re-derivation 'legitimate (the target never moved)' and only a resize against the gates illegitimate, which is the side this lane is on (ADDENDUM-neiso106-prereg-collision-2026-09-06.md). (2) 0.95470 is numerically the scalar neiso-104 declared (0.9547) and reached by a different, later-refuted argument; nothing here depends on that derivation, and the agreement is itself the finding above. (3) The coefficient estimator was one of three computed before choosing (geometric 0.76550, arithmetic-of-per-year 0.76441, log-elasticity 0.75929); the geometric one is declared because the target is a geometric mean, and the choice is immaterial -- the three span scalars 0.95433-0.95470, about 0.03% of price against a +/-10% band. (4) THE STOP RULE IS PRE-COMMITTED: third and last; the coefficient has now been measured on the full span at two depths, so no fourth sizing is legitimate in either direction. || G-CTRL form 4 (the incumbent's committed bundle is the control, no control LP spent), validated by G-DRIFT: the keeper sha 8b2c890d resolves and is an ancestor of HEAD, and all 12 changed solve-path files classify INERT for a NEISO backcast. Ledgered as ONE free parameter under rule 21 [R-DOF] (owner ruling R-AY) whose identification source is the RULING, reported at full magnitude -- a re-derivation of the same knob, not an additional one. market_story: The 4.530% cut moves fossil MARKUP only, so the market story is a merit-order story, not a cost story. CC_REGULAR is NEISO's price-setting class in almost every hour, and cutting its committed/econ bands lowers the offer at which the marginal combined cycle clears -- which is what the whole level shift buys, since NEISO's LMP is a gas-CC LMP. Against the superseded keeper the arm gives back roughly a third of that class's displaced energy (CC_REGULAR -0.0151 TWh in 2025) to CC_CHP (+0.0104) and ST_GAS (+0.0024): a shallower cut leaves the cogeneration and steam-gas offers relatively dearer than the deep cut had made them, so the crossing point moves back up the stack toward where the un-cut neiso-99 recipe had it. CT_PEAKER barely moves (-0.0013 TWh) because its peak band is the ISO-NE offer cap and was never scaled -- the class clears on scarcity, not on markup. Everything outside the four scoped groups is second-order re-dispatch at 0.0017 TWh or less against ~114 TWh of annual load: nothing in the must-run, renewable, hydro or interchange rows is repriced, and none of it is claimed to be.
